root_idea.summary: The root centers on gathering, concentration, and coming together.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop usages for compact masses and groups, as well as turning or casting something down, falling or rolling into a hollow, and directing oneself downward.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form I verb underlying the Quranic passive form.
Displayed as the active participle citation form of Form IV أَكَبَّ.

senses.definition: To cast or throw down upon the face; to prostrate.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is passive and describes faces being cast into the Fire.

senses.definition: Bent or directed face-downward; proceeding prone or with the face toward the ground.
senses.usage_conditions: In مُكِبًّا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ, the active participle describes one walking or advancing with the face lowered toward the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To invert or turn an object over, especially a vessel so that its contents pour out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of turning a vessel, bowl, or other object onto its opening or face.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or wound a camel in the legs.
To wind or convolve thread, hair, or similar material into a ball or compact mass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical or extended usage; the resulting ball is كُبَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be weighty or heavy.
To kindle or set fire to the plant called كُبّ.
To make كباب: small pieces of meat cut up and roasted or broiled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical Form II usage; the food is commonly meat roasted over coals or on skewers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bend or incline oneself downward toward a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Commonly construed with عَلَى or with a directional complement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall, especially after stumbling, or to fall prostrate or prone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence places the stumbling usage alongside the prostrate or face-down usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To set oneself to a task and persist or adhere to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى and an affair, work, or activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For camels to become prostrated by disease or emaciation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is conventionally camels in the cited expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become contracted and compact, especially through moisture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of sand or similar material becoming a compact mass.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wrap oneself up in a garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical usage describing someone bundled or enveloped in clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To press or crowd together upon something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction with عَلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become inverted or turned down so as to pour out contents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a jug or similar vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn or throw something over, one part upon another, or to throw it from a height.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reduplicated Form I expresses repeated or successive overturning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw into a deep place or hollow, with the object tumbling, turning over, or piling upon others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is attested in the Quranic expression فَكُبْكِبُوا فِيهَا; no modern verse location is assigned here because the supplied QAC locations do not include that form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect scattered property or animals by bringing its dispersed parts together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of gathering camels or other wealth by driving them together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect themselves together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or reflexive reduplicated construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant or tree of the ḥamḍ vegetation, useful for kindling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry also records a possible identification with a kind of wild grass.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A forceful charge, onset, impetus, or assault, and the vehemence of such an action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of fighting, a collision or charge between troops or horses, the release of horses to charge or race, the vehemence of winter, and a dash of hellfire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A throwing into a deep place or hollow.
A collected or piled-together mass of dust, earth, or other material.
A ball or compact convolution of spun thread or hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is كُبَبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A congregated company, troop, or main body, especially of horses or men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Can denote the greater number or principal body of a troop.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A herd of large camels.
A family or household dependent upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عَلَيْهِ كُبَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pressing or crowding together.
Weight or bulk imposed upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively in the expression أَلْقَى عَلَيْهِ كُبَّتَهُ, ‘he threw his weight upon him.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: Small pieces of meat roasted or broiled over burning coals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence notes that the word may be Persian in origin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great number of camels, sheep, or goats packed so closely that they mount one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used adjectivally of an exceptionally numerous herd.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dust, earth, adhesive mud, clay, or moist sand compacted into a mass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The material is especially described as moist, cleaving, or compact through moisture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A medicinal substance from China, identified with cubeb.
A particular traditional Arab game.
A man of compact and strong build.
An excellent variety of thick dates.
A closely congregated body of men.
A fat or corpulent woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical entry explicitly uses the feminine human noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who is constantly stumbling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression رَجُلٌ أَكَبُّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who looks frequently toward the ground.
A dust-coloured wheat with thick ears and thick straw.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited variety is described as fodder whose eaters do not become brisk or sprightly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prominent gathered mass or shining body; specifically the main body of water, a visible star, or a gleaming mass or flash.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical discussion also applies it to a boy nearing adolescence because his bodily form is becoming gathered or developed, and to the gleam of a military troop.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form IV discussion.

cautions: The Quranic form كُبْكِبُوا discussed in the lexical evidence is not one of the supplied QAC form groups, so it is preserved as a separate classical lexical item without assigning an unsupported modern Quran location.
The QAC nominal occurrence مُكِبًّا is presented under its active-participle citation form rather than the generic label Noun.
